text:
maria: quick question — several users on the new edge quickstart reported weird "default export" errors when importing the JS SDK in Vite. stack traces reference .default and then runtime crashes. anyone seen this?

alex: yup saw 2 reports this morning. usually manifests like: 
```js
// working in node CJS build?
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
// but in ESM build folks are doing
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
// sometimes you need
import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
```

sam: FWIW, the root cause is often bundler + tsconfig interop flags. if package exports both CJS and ESM but consumers have moduleResolution/interop off, they get the module.exports vs exports.default mismatch. Vite + esbuild tends to prefer ESM and will expect a default.

kevin: Also seen when consumers set "module": "ESNext" but don't enable "esModuleInterop" or "allowSyntheticDefaultImports" in tsconfig. TS transpiles import default to a synthetic default that runtime might not find.

maria: ugh. user reported with edge runtime: `ReferenceError: _default is not defined` after bundling with Vite. they were using our sample app (next-edge + vite plugin).

alex: Two practical options:
1) Docs: clarify recommended import patterns for each runtime/bundler (Vite, Webpack, Bun).
2) SDK: ship a clearer dual export shape and add compatibility note in package.json exports. maybe add `export { default } from './dist/esm/index.js'` and ensure `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs')` for CJS.

sam: We should also add a snippet in the quickstart:
```js
// safe, works in both ESM and CJS with proper ts settings
import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
// or with types in TS
import type { Client } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = (Redwood as any).default ? (Redwood as any).default.createClient() : Redwood.createClient()
```

kevin: I'd rather avoid runtime casts in docs. instead show the tsconfig keys and `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` if you enable esModuleInterop. Example: add this to tsconfig.json: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "moduleResolution": "bundler"
  }
}
```

maria: Good call. And add a short table: bundler -> recommended import form -> tsconfig flags. That should cut down support tickets.

kevin: Is there any runtime-specific oddness for edge (Cloudflare/Netlify) aside from bundler behavior?

sam: Edge runtimes sometimes rewrite imports during deploy or like Netlify plugin rewrites and can drop `.default` wrappers. But mostly it's upstream bundler. For Cloudflare workers, people using @vercel/ncc or esbuild might get different module interop behavior.

docs-bot: Reminder: we have an existing doc page at https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/js/interop (staged). It currently mentions ESM/CJS but doesn't show tsconfig examples or Vite quirks.

maria: I'll open a docs PR to add: recommended imports, tsconfig snippets, Vite + Next edge note, and a sample minimal repro repo link. Who can review?

alex: happy to review the wording and add a short troubleshooting checklist (+1 for adding a code snippet that checks for `.default`).

kevin: I'll file a tiny SDK change to adjust package.json exports and add a compatibility test in CI that bundles with esbuild/vite and runs quickstart on a mock edge runtime. PR later today.

maria: awesome. can someone triage the user support threads and post repro artifacts here if they have them? link them in the PR description.

deploy-bot: New deploy queued: staging-docs (maria) - build 4721.

sam: quick note — also add a one-liner about TypeScript `import type` for types-only imports to avoid loading runtime values in edge. e.g. `import type { Client } from '@redwood/inference'` + `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` when needed.

maria: perfect. I'll push the docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2467 and tag reviewers. thanks all :party_parrot: 

alex: thanks — this should cut a lot of noise. cc @support to watch for followups.
